title: Heliotrope peak-surge capacity notes (scratch)
content:
Call notes: Heliotrope Retail — peak surge handling (scratch)

Date: 2025-01-23 (initial call) / follow-up 2025-02-10
Owner: Leah Chen (CS) — working notes, not polished
Attendees (Heliotrope): Maia Rivers (SRE), Ben Kline (Platform), Jasmine Park (Product)
Attendees (Redwood): Leah Chen (CS), Aaron Patel (Solutions), Marcos Silva (Infra SE)

Background / Why this matters
- Heliotrope runs an in-store checkout recommender and a post-purchase conversational assistant. Both see predictable daily peak windows (17:30–19:30 local store time) and occasional marketing-driven spikes.
- Current prototype on single-host private deployment hit p95 latency > 600ms during promo spikes — unacceptable for checkout flow.
- They want a plan for production-grade peak capacity: predictable latency SLOs, bounded cost, and operational runbook for escalation.

Goals (customer stated)
- Maintain p95 gen latency <= 250ms for checkout recommendation requests during peak (small prompt + 64-token gen).
- Support 4x baseline sustained request rate during peak and 6x transient bursts up to 15 minutes.
- Keep per-token cost growth under 2.5x compared to baseline during peaks (budget cap).
- Region-aware routing: US-East primary, EU-West secondary for EU customers (data residency + GDPR).

Current infra / constraints
- Using a quantized 13B open model in-house (mixed int8). Memory footprint ~28GB with KV cache overhead unpredictable across sessions.
- Edge clients send short sequences (~40 tokens prompt + up to 64 tokens gen). Sequence distribution skewed to short, but occasional chat history increases seq to 512 tokens.
- No dedicated pre-warm schedule. Instances spin up on demand -> cold-KV cache and high initial latency.
- Limited observability into per-token cost and fine-grained batching at present.

Key technical notes / gotchas observed in call
- Cold KV cache after pod recycling leads to 2-3x higher latency for the first 10–20 requests per model shard. For short-lived bursts this dominates.
- Dynamic batching helps throughput but can add jitter to p95 if not latency-capped. Need batching policy that prioritizes p95 over absolute throughput during checkout endpoints.
- Quantization artifacts: some prompt templates used by Heliotrope are syntactically fragile (product codes, SKUs). Quan–int8 variants occasionally mis-surface formatting; require evaluation set checks.
- Tokenization cost mismatch: their checkout prompts include long product descriptions pulled from CMS; tokenization can bloat per-request tokens by 1.8x compared to naive estimate.
- Multi-region routing: they need strict EU data residency. Any fallback path must ensure EU requests never cross to US compute.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: checkout UI expects near-instant suggestion (first token matters). Streaming reduces perceived latency but complicates batching fallbacks.

Recommended architecture (sketch, high-level)
- Dedicated capacity pool in each region (US-East, EU-West). Reserve baseline capacity sized for 4x sustained peak with headroom for warm-up.
- Pre-warm window: autoscale policy to scale-up 30–45 minutes before known daily peak (cron + telemetry signal). For marketing events, a webhook trigger from Heliotrope to pre-warm.
- Burst reserve: enable short-term burst capacity (burst queue) to absorb 6x peaks for up to 15 minutes (fail closed to canary quantized fallback if exceeded).
- Batching policy: continuous batching with p95 latency cap of 150ms for checkout route; use smaller batch-size cap for checkout route and larger for background assistant route.
- Prefix/KV caching: persist hot prefix keys across pods in Dedicated pool (sticky cache / warm restore) to reduce cold-run penalty. Consider memcached-backed prefix cache at the Dedicated layer.
- Fallback strategy: primary = quantized 13B (fast); fallback = 7B int4 for emergency (lower quality). Define automatic rollbacks and quality gate based on checks against a small eval prompt-set.

Operational playbook snippets (explicit)
- Metrics to monitor: tokens/sec per-shard, batch sizes (median/p95), KV miss rate, GPU memory pressure, p50/p95/p99 latency for checkout route, model-output quality score (synthetic evals).
- Alert thresholds: p95 > 300ms for >2 minutes -> page SRE; KV miss rate > 30% -> investigate pod churn; quality regressions (eval score drop > 4%) -> auto-fallback and page ML eng.
- Runbook quick steps for surge: 1) Verify pre-warm completed, 2) If p95 high, reduce batch cap for checkout route (immediate), 3) If GPU mem pressure high, trigger burst pool add or shift traffic to fallback model, 4) If quality drop, roll back to previous model variant and open incident.

Cost/quality trade-offs (notes to discuss in PoC)
- Pre-warming increases baseline cost (charged when reserved). Need to simulate cost across entire store fleet vs better batching.
- Caching reduces tokens and GPU work but adds complexity and state to restore across restarts. There's a tradeoff between persistent cache cost and per-token compute cost.
- Fallback to smaller model reduces cost but may introduce subtle UX regressions; must validate on Heliotrope SKU-format prompts.

PoC plan (small, timeboxed)
- Scope: US-East checkout route only, 2-week PoC. Measure p95 under synthetic daily peak profile + 2 marketing spike templates.
- Components: Dedicated pool (3-4 gpus sized for 4x), pre-warm cron, KV prefix cache experiment, batching policy with latency cap, synthetic traffic harness (Aaron), evaluation set (Heliotrope to provide 20 representative prompts).
- Success criteria: p95 <= 250ms during peak sustained; token-cost multiplier <= 2.5x vs baseline; KV-miss rate < 15% after warm-up.

Action items (who / by when)
- Leah: craft PoC brief + SOW draft for Heliotrope (due 2025-01-30).
- Aaron: build synthetic peak traffic harness and baseline runner (due 2025-02-03).
- Marcos: prototype prefix cache warm-restore and measure cold-run penalty on current infra (due 2025-02-05).
- Heliotrope (Maia/Ben): share 20 representative checkout prompts + marketing spike schedule (due 2025-01-28).
- Tanya: prepare short eval harness to catch quantization regressions on SKU formatting (due 2025-02-04).

Open questions / follow-ups (to resolve in technical deep-dive)
- Can Heliotrope commit to sending a webhook for planned marketing events to trigger pre-warm? (If not, we need a predictive traffic-based pre-warm.)
- Are there any strict PII fields embedded in prompts that require token masking before sending to hosted inference? Need legal check.
- What is acceptable latency for streaming-first-token vs complete generation? UI may prefer first-token < 80ms. Can we meet that with current model variants?
- Confirm EU-data-residency constraints: does conversation context need to be stored beyond ephemeral session?

Notes to self (personal scratch)
- Watch for memory fragmentation during repeated autoscale cycles (seen in other retail customers). If fragmentation high, consider pinned model instances and request-level routing instead of frequent scale-in/outs.
- Bring up embedding reuse for rerank cache — storing top-10 candidates embeddings could avoid recompute during burst.
- Validate tokenization inflation on product descriptions: ask Heliotrope to send 50 raw CMS snippets to run tokenizer locally.

Next sync: schedule 30–45m technical deep-dive 2025-01-29 (target) to align infra team and get SOW sign-off.

-- end of scratch --

(Will convert to a cleaner PoC brief once Heliotrope shares prompts and we have infra measurements.)
